va_fort_windham_rocks.blurb: Fort Windham Rocks is a small boulder-problem spot in the North District of Shenandoah National Park, a short walk off the Appalachian Trail. Two big split boulders rise roughly 50 feet, with cracks and gaps between them, and the twelve problems here are short and mostly friendly: a handful of very easy lines, a cluster around V1 and V2, and just a couple of harder ones, topping out near V5. Holds are jugs on the easier lines, and some tops have a steep drop just beyond the lip, so spot carefully. It suits a quick, relaxed outing or a family hike with a little scrambling.
va_fort_windham_rocks.parking_note: Leave the car at the Compton Gap parking area on Skyline Drive, near mile 10.4, then walk from there.
va_fort_windham_rocks.approach: From the Compton Gap parking area, follow the Appalachian Trail north, turn onto the Dickey Ridge Trail, and the rocks appear on the right after a few hundred yards. About 0.8 miles round trip.

va_belly_boulder.blurb: Belly Boulder sits in the Roanoke area on the McAfee's Knob side of Southwest Virginia, in one of the sunniest bouldering zones on the mountain. It holds twelve problems, from easy V0 slabs and arches up through a solid block of V3s, with a few real tests at V4, V6 and V7. The climbing leans on crimps, slopers, sidepulls and the occasional jug. You reach it by walking past the neighbouring Project Boulder, so it pairs well with the other blocks nearby for a day of bouldering.

va_raven_s_roost_cliff.blurb: Raven's Roost Cliff is a roped crag below the Raven's Roost Overlook on the Blue Ridge Parkway, around mile 10.7 near Charlottesville. A dozen lines split evenly between trad and top rope, running from easy 5.4 up through the middle 5.x grades, with a pair in the 5.8 and 5.9 range and a couple of hard outliers near 5.11 and 5.13. Many lines are well suited to top roping, but anchors can be awkward and thin, so bring plenty of webbing. Expect some loose rock and litter at the base.
va_raven_s_roost_cliff.parking_note: Park at the Raven's Roost Overlook on the Blue Ridge Parkway; the cliff lies just below it.
